sessions.phase_label: Initial developmental edits and client review

requirements.title: Developmental Editorial Letter
requirements.definition: Provide a 15–20 page editorial letter with a detailed overview of the novel, analysis of its elements and movement, examples, and revision resources.
requirements.boundary_note: Length, analytical contents, examples, resources, and the stated July 20 delivery date are attributes of one letter deliverable rather than separate Requirements.

unresolved_candidates.description: The client's goal of creating mystery and a sense of the unknown may be an editorial acceptance criterion, but the message frames it primarily as the client's own revision intention rather than a clear independent request to the freelancer.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Just seeing this. 
I'm on vacation so I will read through the comments and then sit with them. I'll be more focused once I get home anyway. 
I just read through the first few pages and comments. I get what you're saying and look forward to discussing some of this in more detail. Some of the things I did were intentional, but obviously not effective. I can explain when we meet and I see your full notes/letter. This is really helpful because I think I need to find other ways to create a sense of mystery and the unknown. 

We can talk more later, but I know this will be very helpful. Lots of work to do...and questions to ask. :) 

Bela

contents: detailed overview of the novel's elements
analysis of the movement of the novel

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Good morning (here on the East Coast),

I quickly read through your letter last night and going to take my time and through everything today.

It’s incredibly helpful. Even going through quickly I understood a lot of what you meant.

I can meet almost any time in the afternoon, some mornings are busier for me. If you could, I’d like to meet sooner rather than later. I do have questions about the structure, mostly in the beginning and then would like some clarity on other things you mention.

I think I’ve decided to self-publish. It’s so hard to get an agent, although I do have a couple of indie presses on my list. I did send out some feelers to agents for fun before I had the manuscript edited. Nothing so far, a few nos, but at least rejections took a while. Plus, trad publishing will take forever, I lose control of my work, I still have to do my own marketing... I’d love to hear your take on this. I know how hard it is to get published traditionally and I don’t want to waste time. My book is about my words and my message. Sure, I’d love to make money from it, but that’s not my primary goal. Publishing without an agent, maybe…but it has to be the right place.

Social media is buzzing with data center talk and protests (and AI). I feel something in my gut, but I don’t know if it’s anxiety or excitement. I’d like to get this published as soon as possible – the time is so right. Of course, I want it to be as perfect as possible.

Where do I go from here, once we’re done and I make all of my changes? Is a copyedit enough after this? Money is a bit tight, but I will figure it out. Just need to budget for copyedit, cover, interior format.

Do you have recommendations, particularly a cover designer? Maybe they also do interior formatting. Copyediting will be key, because I’ve added many scenes based on your earlier comments.

I know I’m getting ahead of everything. I feel a pull.

I can meet tomorrow in the afternoon or early evening after 1pm EST, but before 8 pm EST, Thursday and Friday, any time before 4pm EST, Saturday any time after 12pm EST…the following week I am less flexible – can meet Monday between 1pm and 4pm EST, Tuesday anytime.

FYI, I’ve added about 15k words, mostly new scenes, more info about Matt, more details about the world, more character development, esp. for everyone (the men, Sophie). There will be deletions also. That’s one reason why I need to figure out the next editing steps!

You are amazing! Just wanted to tell you that.

Bela

execution.observed_behavior: The client reports reading the delivered letter, finding it incredibly helpful, and understanding much of its guidance.

human_review.decision_note: Message 2 refers to the expected notes or letter but does not itself state the annotated length and contents; message 1 must be reviewed to determine whether it is the proper introduction source or an unambiguously accepted proposal.
